items.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns; Colette Kress named interim CEO
items.summary: Nvidia announced a CEO transition in an SEC 8-K filing, with Jensen Huang resigning after reports of a board investigation into personal conduct, CFO Colette Kress stepping in as interim CEO, and Harvey C. Jones named the company's first-ever board chair. The leadership shakeup at the world's most valuable chipmaker lands days before Nvidia's Q3 FY2027 earnings and amid intense scrutiny of AI infrastructure spending.

items.headline: Anthropic sets IPO price range, launches Nasdaq roadshow under ticker ANT
items.summary: Anthropic launched the roadshow for its planned IPO, targeting $70-$78 per Class A share plus a $26 billion private placement from chip and cloud partners, with pricing expected around November 18 and trading to begin under 'ANT' soon after. It would rank among the largest-ever AI sector listings, following the company's October S-1 filing that disclosed fast-growing revenue alongside large losses.

items.headline: SoftBank posts ~$7 billion quarterly loss on US AI data center writedown
items.summary: SoftBank swung to a large net loss after taking a roughly $3.7 billion charge tied to realigned power-equipment plans for its US AI data center projects, plus an Intel share slide and higher financing costs. Analysts cite it as an early sign of risk in the aggressive buildout of AI infrastructure that SoftBank and peers have bet heavily on.

items.headline: OpenAI winds down Cursor's access to its models after SpaceX acquisition
items.summary: OpenAI is cutting off model access for the AI coding tool Cursor, now owned by Anysphere after SpaceX's acquisition, with the contract winding down around November 12 and future OpenAI models withheld entirely. Cursor's CEO said OpenAI models made up only about 5% of its traffic, and users can still reach them via personal API keys.

items.headline: Google DeepMind launches Gemini Robotics 2.5 for humanoid partners
items.summary: DeepMind released Gemini Robotics 2.5, its most capable vision-language-action model yet, rolling it out to robotics partners including Apptronik, Agile Robots and Boston Dynamics. Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz are reportedly piloting Apollo 2 humanoids on an active auto production line using the model.

items.headline: Anthropic ships Claude Fable 5.2 and restricted Claude Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic made Claude Fable 5.2 generally available across its platforms with faster coding and reasoning at lower API cost, while the more capable Claude Mythos 5.2 remains restricted to vetted organizations through life-sciences and cybersecurity verification programs due to its higher-risk profile.

items.headline: AI hardware-testing startup Nominal raises $240M Series C at $3B valuation
items.summary: Nominal, which builds an AI platform for hardware engineering and testing, raised $240 million led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Insight Partners, tripling its valuation to $3 billion in eight months. The round follows a $71.2 million US Air Force award tied to Collaborative Combat Aircraft work.

items.headline: Generative media platform fal raises $1.3B+ at $16B valuation
items.summary: fal disclosed a combined $1.65 billion across Series E and Series F rounds, with the Series F led by Bessemer Venture Partners and backed by Nvidia, doubling its valuation to $16 billion since April. The company provides infrastructure for running generative image and video models at scale.

items.headline: Agility Robotics goes public on Nasdaq as AGLT via SPAC merger
items.summary: Agility Robotics completed its merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI and began trading on Nasdaq, raising roughly $465 million in gross proceeds to fund its Digit humanoid robot and expand manufacturing, becoming one of the first pure-play humanoid robot makers to go public.

items.headline: Humble Robotics raises $51M Series A for cabless autonomous freight trucks
items.summary: Humble Robotics, founded by self-driving veterans from Apple and Uber, raised a $51 million Series A led by Obvious Ventures to scale its cabless, autonomous electric freight vehicles, bringing total funding to $75 million ahead of planned 2027 customer pilots.

items.headline: Meta releases Muse Ember, a small efficient model for AI agent workloads
items.summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs launched Muse Ember, its smallest and most cost-efficient Muse model, aimed at repetitive agentic subtasks like tool calls, coding and document extraction, with a context window over one million tokens, pairing with the larger Muse Wonder model for higher-level planning.

items.headline: Apple begins charging for extra AI usage with Intelligence Usage Packs
items.summary: Apple introduced its first paid AI add-on, a one-time $49.99 'Intelligence Usage Pack' letting Creator Studio subscribers buy extra cloud AI capacity after hitting monthly limits, currently limited to Logic Pro, signaling a shift toward directly monetizing AI compute.

items.headline: Google unveils TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max chips for the 'agentic era'
items.summary: Google Cloud introduced two new eighth-generation TPUs: 8tx, aimed at secure and confidential inference plus small-scale training, and 8i Max, which doubles compute, memory and bandwidth over TPU 8i for massive-context workloads, pushing its alternative to Nvidia GPUs for large-scale AI infrastructure.

items.headline: Australia plans dedicated AI safety regulator after government breach
items.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced plans for mandatory AI safety standards and a new regulator with power to penalize frontier AI companies, including mandatory incident reporting and independent model evaluation, following a breach of a government Medicare statistics site involving an OpenAI agent.
